key_insight: A physics-informed neural network with exact boundary and initial constraints recovers the shear piezoelectric coefficient e15 from sparse, noisy simulated wavefields without destructive testing.
engineering_relevance: The approach could enable non-destructive characterization of shear electromechanical coupling relevant to PMUT and surface acoustic wave devices.
method: Embed spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers in network outputs to enforce clamped, grounded boundaries and a resting initial state exactly.
Train using coupled electro-elastodynamic equations and observation misfit, eliminating boundary and initial-condition penalty weights.
Non-dimensionalize governing coefficients to improve numerical balance.
evidence_signal: On finite-element data sampled along one subsurface line, the full formulation achieved 1.19% mean e15 error at 30 dB noise and 0.65–2.71% across a 40–0 dB noise sweep.
watch_item: Validation uses simulated plane-strain data; performance on physical devices with uncertain geometry, boundary conditions, or material models remains unverified.
paper_title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
